behavior: Initial scope, pending amendments, task refinement and mandatory research obligations
boundary: Simple-objective classification and whether user text authorizes a particular action remain semantic heuristics.

behavior: Mechanical and independent audit gates, failures, budget-error classification and repair threshold
boundary: Correct evidence interpretation is an external model judgment; a structural verdict is not a scientific proof.

behavior: Single selected goal, FIFO creation, approved advancement and resume ordering
boundary: Three goals; explicit user selection and arbitrary queue lengths rely on implementation tests.

behavior: Session binding, clear, panel state, owner lease rotation and stale callbacks; verified goals clear after a real input, with final usage preserved
boundary: No proof of host event delivery, SHA collision resistance, PID reuse or cross-host liveness.

behavior: Lock/read/validate/append, hash-chain deltas with periodic snapshots, in-memory snapshot reuse, revision parent continuity, partial tails and atomic legacy import
boundary: Filesystem operations, mkdir exclusivity, successful fsync and atomic rename are assumptions; no power-loss proof. Empty crash locks can require operator recovery.

behavior: Read-only scope gate, explicit network/install overrides, exact grant cache and stale confirmation fences
boundary: Command classification is a conservative heuristic, not a shell security boundary. Hash identity, host restrictions and filesystem races are external.

behavior: Metered components, final turn accounting, cumulative budget, no-progress count and resume preservation
boundary: Actual provider usage can arrive late, be unknown or overshoot the budget; no monetary hard cap. Accounting model uses positive known costs; implementation enumeration includes non-finite inputs.

behavior: Pending input priority, completed host outcome, required tools, budget/stagnation gates and idle release
boundary: Host fairness and tool response assumptions; no unconditional termination or long-run stability proof. Prospective next-goal gates are abstract Booleans.

behavior: Regenerate current session/goal snapshots and one eligible policy, preserving conversation and valid queued planning
boundary: Checks control-message structure and identity, not whether an LLM obeys the text or correctly interprets a summary.

behavior: Declared per-goal verification environment (read-only/ephemeral workspace, isolated/allowlist/open proxy egress), frozen snapshots, fail-closed sandboxing, cancellation/identity gates and environment-vs-implementation failure classification
boundary: MicroVMs, private Docker engines, proxy enforcement and process delivery remain integration assumptions. Failure classification is a conservative heuristic that never converts a failed check into a pass; environment advice does not prove the failure was environmental.

behavior: Artifact path boundary, successful inspection, later response and complete unique findings
boundary: Path model abstracts canonicalization; concurrent symlink mutation, filesystem stability and paged content meaning are outside it. audit_record/list alone do not count as inspection.

behavior: Current policy precedence, retired limits ignored and exact two-release host support
boundary: Current and immediately preceding release only. Old goal data protection is separate from host-version support.

behavior: Status labels, Unicode/control cleanup, width/height bounds and pending proposal display; readable complete approval summaries with bounded scrollable review
boundary: Host width utilities and tested terminal semantics assumed; no pixel, color-contrast or full accessibility proof.

behavior: Docker Sandboxes verification backend, frozen input manifests, private runner, cancellation cleanup and lease recovery
boundary: Unit, proxy and fake CLI regressions plus a separately recorded real microVM acceptance suite. No formal composition proof: sbx, Docker, image integrity, filesystem stability, upstream DNS/policies, process delivery and watchdog survival remain external assumptions. See docs/docker-sandboxes-acceptance.md for the bounded tested cases.

behavior: Diagnosis quality, free-text prompts, remote tools and scientific/product correctness
boundary: Semantic content and external systems lack a closed finite specification; retained as explicit exclusions, not claimed verified.
